strengths: Novel insight on optimizer state misalignment in LoRA with well-motivated theoretical framing (Section 2.1, Eq. 3)
Comprehensive experimental evaluation across language (commonsense, math, code) and vision domains with multiple model scales (7B-70B), unusual depth on low-rank regimes (r=1,2,4)
Strong empirical results especially at low ranks: 40% improvement over DoRA at r=4, LoFT@r=8 matches LoRA@r=64 on code generation
Solid theoretical contributions (Lemmas 1-2) showing exact recovery for matrix factorization; first low-rank method provably recovering full fine-tuning in full-rank limit
Practical design: eliminates LoRA scaling hyperparameter α, LoFT(simple) variant achieves 5-6% memory overhead, consistent improvements across 3 LLaMA generations
Excellent reproducibility: detailed algorithms, hyperparameters in appendix, code availability promised, clear ablations validating each design component
Training dynamics (Figures 5, 10) demonstrate LoFT closely tracks full fine-tuning from early iterations, indicating fundamental alignment rather than just final convergence
weaknesses: Significant practical overhead limits adoption in efficiency-constrained settings: 25.65% memory increase (Table 8), 2.26-3.23× training latency (Table 12) despite efficiency claims for LoRA
Theoretical-practical gap: Lemmas 1-2 apply to matrix factorization and GD, not to the AdamW algorithm actually used; convergence analysis and formal recovery guarantees missing
Inconsistent ablation results undermine design justification: LoFT without alternation outperforms full LoFT on ViT-B (91.60% vs 91.18%, Table 6), suggesting over-engineering
Marginal vision improvements lack explanation: Table 3 shows <1% gains on medical imaging within noise margins; stark contrast to 2-11% language gains unexplored

Method complexity may hinder adoption: six tightly coupled components (projections, Kronecker/Khatri-Rao products, calibration matrices) with subtle numerical stability requirements (ill-conditioned matrices not analyzed)
Limited novelty over concurrent work: AltLoRA (Yu et al., 2025) proposes similar alternating optimization independently, suggesting alternation's value is straightforward
Hyperparameter 'elimination' overstated: α fixed as α=r but rank r still tuned; method introduces new tuning surfaces (calibration design choices, alternation schedule not validated for sensitivity)
Rank constraint r ≤ √min{m,n} for memory efficiency may be restrictive for large models; expressivity-efficiency trade-off not analyzed
Missing analysis of when LoFT underperforms and failure modes; why does LLaMA-3 gain smaller improvements than LLaMA-7B (Table 2)?
